articleTitle: Improved of Dynamic Torque by Field Oriented Control based Fuzzy Logic for BLDC Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper proposed a brushless DC motor control model using magnetic field orientation combined with fuzzy logic control (FOC-FZ: Field Oriented Control-Fuzzy Logic Control) in order to minimize the torque fluctuation when changing operating state in the quadrants of the electric drive system such as acceleration, deceleration, starting and reversing operation. The simulation results shown that the FOC-FZ method has many advantages compared to other control methods. Torque oscillations are greatly reduced, dynamic and steady-state responses of motor's speed and torque are highly improved. The FOC-FZ method is well suited for applications in transmission/drive systems with high stability, accuracy, and fast response.

articleTitle: An investigation of the Internet-based approach for drone management in a city environment
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Today, with the exponential growth of numerous drone operations ranging from infrastructure monitoring to even package delivery services, drone management regarding the use of drones in urban planning plays an essential role in smart cities' sustainable development. Besides, with the rapid growth of technologies, especially computing, sensing, the Internet of things (IoT), and Information and Communication Technologies (ICT), drone demand has increased in real-world applications. However, the larger the number of operating drones, the more accidents in the sky. Therefore, it is essential to manage drones in traffic flows. This study presents an overview of drone management methods in a city environment, presenting the Internet-based approach to drone management in urban areas. Through the control station on the ground, the drone user can set up a flight trajectory and send it to the drone via the Internet. This method allows the user to control and monitor the drone. This method is practiced and validated through a Quadrotor and D-com Viettel 4G test.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification Knee Osteoarthritis Algorithm using YOLOv3 and VGG-16 Models
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The paper proposes an algorithm to help doctors identify Knee Osteoarthritis automatically on X-ray images by deep learning method with the YOLOv3 model and VGG-16. We collect data including 2874 knee X-ray images taken from the OAI dataset which is a large data set of Knees and joints. In this paper, all data are labeled and tested by chiropractors at Bach Mai Hospital which will be preprocessed by applying the CLAHE algorithm to improve image quality. Next, the YOLOv3 modelis trained with a preprocessed dataset as input. It then predicts the location of the knee joint on the X-ray image automatically. Finally, we use VGG-16 to classify the image. Besides, we alsouse preprocessing methods to enhance the image quality before training, and thus the accuracy of the problem is also significantly improved. The results display that the proposed method achievesan accuracy of up to 89%

articleTitle: Adaptive strategy with output constraints for multi-section web linkage system
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Solving unpredictable fluctuations in tension and speed is essential for optimizing the material transportation process of web materials linkage systems. We develop an adaptive controller to control the output values and restraint tension values within a specific range of requirements. External disturbances existing in this nonlinear system are estimated by the radial basis function neural network (RBF NN), while tension output constraints maintenance and stability of object are both guaranteed by Barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) analysis. The superiority of the proposed controller compared with other nonlinear controllers is verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Distinguish normal white blood cells from leukemia cells by detection, classification, and counting blood cells using YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Leukemia is a group of blood cancers that usually begin in the bone marrow and result in high numbers of abnormal blood cells. Distinguishing normal white blood cells from leukemia cells plays a role in the diagnosis of blood diseases. Over the years, manual methods can detect, classify, and count blood cells that are labor-intensive slow, time-consuming, subject to error, and costly. An automatic system is applied in the processing detection through microscopic images that will be fast, cheap, and high accuracy without special needs of equipment for lab testing. In this paper, we propose a method of detection, classification, and counting to distinguish five types of normal white blood cells (WBCs) from abnormal white blood cells (leukemia) using the You Only Look Once version 5 (YOLOv5) to aid the diagnosis of blood diseases. After using the YOLOv5 algorithm, we manually labeled the blood cells, and the leukemia cells labeled are the largest with 619 cells, while the number of normal WBCs labeled is a basophil, 115 neutrophils, 23 eosinophils, 80 lymphocytes, and 73 monocytes, respectively. The tested result with the average accuracy of detection and classification of the blood cells is 93.0%.

articleTitle: A study on temperature in the classroom using the statistical methodology to predict the effect on the comfortable of students due to pandemics
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this study, the factors of optimizing the temperature distribution of the air-conditioned room are based on experiments to provide analysis and evaluation to choose the best option for comfort zones. By using reputable testing methods in statistics: Taguchi, ANOVA, and supporting software in model building (SOLIDWORK), numerical and statistical software (MINITAB), from there, conducting experiments and data processing. The research has given the optimal factors for the air-conditioned room temperature field, including room temperature measurement plan (P1), time to measure room temperature (P2), value setting of the temperature for the indoor unit (P3), and final indoor unit fan speed (P4). After performing experiments, verifying, and using statistical analysis methods, the optimal model results for the room temperature field are P12P23P31P43 (Option of room temperature measurement plan P12 (Option 2), time to measure room temperature P23 (15h), value setting of temperature for indoor unit P31 (22°C), indoor unit fan speed P43 (Level 3)). In which the temperature setting for the indoor unit (C) has the greatest impact. The study has given the optimal factors for the conditioned room temperature distribution. In addition, the study also made predictions to meet the comfort zone of the students sitting inside the air-conditioned room, to offer layout and arrangement options suitable for the epidemic period.

articleTitle: Static Properties and Fatigue Strength of Wire Arc Additive Manufactured 316L
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The use of direct energy deposition (DED) has become much more common recently and in the future the DED technology will be used even more widely. Wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) technology has become much more widespread because it can be done cost-effectively with normal cold metal transfer (CMT) welding equipment. There is still a lack of information on the fatigue strength of parts made with different welding wires. This paper focuses on the mechanical properties of AISI 316L WAAM printed parts as well as bending fatigue strength. The average microhardness values were measured along the build direction. The optical microscope and EBSD detector were used to investigate the microstructure. The tensile strength and bending fatigue strength of the WAAM printed 316L were evaluated. The EBSD investigation revealed that due to high heat input of the WAAM process, the remelting of each consecutive deposited layer caused epitaxial grain growth in the structure, leading to coarse columnar grain structure. There were no visible pores in the microstructure of the WAAM 316L. The hardness of the WAAM 316L was homogenous in the build direction. Based on tensile strength tests, the strength in the deposition direction was greater than in the build direction which is explained by the anisotropy generated in the deposition. The results revealed that the fatigue limit of the WAAM 316L is comparable to that of 316L sheet metal. The fatigue strength of the WAAM 316L was significantly higher in the high cycle fatigue regime compared to the fatigue strength of the powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) printed 316L.

articleTitle: Neural Network PID Controller for PMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The design of MLP NN (Multilayer perceptron neural network) self-tuning PID controller for PMSM drive is proposed in this paper. To cope with the system and external load uncertainly, a self-tuning PID controller using MLP NN is adopted and derived for PMSM drive. MLP is used to identify the plant first. Then the Jacobian information of controlled plant obtained by MLP NN identification is used to adjust the gain of PID controller. A robust parameters self-tuning learning algorithm is used to train the NN for fast convergence. Simulation results show that the proposed controller has the adaptability, strong robustness and satisfactory control performance in PMSM servo system.

articleTitle: Application of Edge Detection Algorithm for Self-Driving Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Self-driving vehicle is not one simple technology but rather a huge system integrating many technologies, which means that the algorithm of autonomous driving is a challenging task. Indeed, most existing autonomous driving classes focus on one of the technologies involved. Vehicle detection road would be contributed algorithm in this process. Various classes of vehicles are to be detected from the surveillance video, and then they need to be classified based on various feature points. This paper brings out the edge detection methods used for vehicle detection from a camera. Lane edge detection is an important foundation in the development of Self-Driving vehicles.

articleTitle: Application of the lean method in designing the layout of face mask manufacturing plants for the prevention of covid-19
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The prolonged global coronavirus pandemic (Covid-19) has affected all aspects of life, economy, and society, especially small and medium businesses. To meet this challenge, many companies are transforming models and reorganizing production and operations to adapt to this situation. These companies have adopted a variety of philosophies to remove non-value-added activities from their production processes to maintain efficiency, flexibility, and profitability. In the context of Industry 4.0, solutions are ready to combine automation technology together with the Lean manufacturing approach. Furthermore, when it comes to efficient use of resources (financial, labor, materials, machine, and equipment), Industry 4.0 should be applied to Lean Processes. Thus, this article shows how to apply the Lean method to optimize plant design to cut waste, improve the efficiency of input resources, increase labor productivity by reducing labor costs, waiting (man-to-man; man-machine), reduced movement, and redundancy of operations in the workflow. Especially, the paper uses the SLP (Systematic Layout Planning) method to arrange the areas, material flow, and supply chain in the factory, Lean application to visualize the factory and combines IoT (Internet of Things). Moreover, using automation and Lean Production theory will support much for factory construction in the future, minimizing irrationalities when applied in practice. The result of the paper will mention a case study on the design and simulation of a face mask plant

articleTitle: Using ground granulated blast furnace slag and fly ash to improve the resistance of fine-grained concrete to sulfuric acid attack
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper presents study using ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) and fly ash (FA) as partial replacement of cement to improve the resistance of fine-grained concrete (FGC) to sulfuric acid attack. Two series of FGC were prepared with W/B ratios of 0.36 and 0.32. In each series: 1 mixture of control FGC, 2 mixtures were investigated: FGC using 40% GGBFS as partial replacement of cement (GS40) and FGC using a combination of 35% GGBFS and 20% FA as partial replacement of cement (GS35FA20). The study results in water environment showed that the compressive strength and the flexural strength of FGC were highest with GS40, the lowest absorption with FGC using GS35FA20 at all experimental ages. The study results in acid environment showed that compressive strength, flexural strength of FGC were highest and the absorption was lowest with a replacement rate of GS35FA20 at 90 days. Control FGC has the lowest acid resistance when compared to FGC using GS40 and FGC using GS35FA20.

articleTitle: Medical Image Segmentation Using Deep Learning and Blending Loss
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Semantic segmentation is an important task in medical-supporting. The purpose of semantic segmentation í to identify pre-defined objects, and its pixel-by-pixel location. The most popular method in semantic segmentation was using Convolutional neural network which has considerably improved semantic image segmentation. This work investigates a Blending loss which incorporates into traditional methods. Three popular algorithms are U-Net, PSPNet and FPN are examined carefully to investigate upgrading performance after combining new objective function. Moreover, we did experiments on two medical datasets to avoid bias and verify performance of the new method.

articleTitle: Analysis of operating conditions of the semi-automatic patient transfer device
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Semi-automated patient transfer devices are essential in health facilities. Especially for patients with limited mobility. Improper patient transfer or poorly designed transfer equipment will cause unnecessary injury to both the patient and the medical staff. In this paper, we choose to solve the problem of working conditions of one of the current patient transfer devices with the aim of ensuring the safety of the device. Three problems are posed including: Center of gravity distribution to avoid overturning - Simulation of natural frequencies - Durability for critical locations. The results show that the structure of the product ensures safe working conditions for users.

articleTitle: Comparison of Polishing Methods: The Effect on The Surface Roughness and Fatigue Performance of PBF-LB manufactured 316L Stainless Steel
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Stainless steel 316L is currently one of the most prominent materials on the AM industry including the laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) manufacturing. The surface roughness of the PBF-LB manufactured material is typically over 10 μm in terms of Ra and this can have a detrimental role in the fatigue resistance of the parts. However, several techniques and machines are now available to reduce the surface roughness, but no comprehensive data is available on the limits or the effectiveness of those. In this paper, the performance of four commonly available techniques is analyzed utilizing equal PBF-LB manufactured 316L samples. The results show the effect on the surface roughness and also the surface profiles and topographies are analyzed. Up to 80% reduction in the surface roughness R<inf>a</inf> could be reached. Moreover, the effect of each polishing method on the fatigue performance in bending fatigue testing was analyzed. The results showed that the fatigue limit of the 316L can be tripled even when mirror finish is not reached.

articleTitle: Vibration analysis of functionally graded beams in thermal environments using an inverse trigonometric shear deformation theory
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The thermal effects on vibration analysis of functionally graded (FG) beams using an inverse trigonometric shear deformation theory are presented in this paper. The present work is based on a higher-order shear deformation theory which accounts for an inverse trigonometric distribution of transverse shear stress and higher-order variation of in-plane and out-of-plane displacements. Lagrange's equations are used to derive motion equations. The Ritz solution method is used to solve problems with different boundary conditions (BCs). In this study, numerical findings for the natural frequencies of functionally graded beams are compared with those from prior research. Changes in power-law index and temperature are explored in relation to the findings.

articleTitle: Significance of Risks in Transportation Projects in Vietnam through two main Dimensions
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Risk in transportation projects is a common and serious problem recently, affecting project objectives such as causing cost increases, delays in progress, unsatisfactory quality and conflicts in relationships among stakeholders. In particular, these risks often occur during the project construction phase, which is the most complex phase and includes many works. In Vietnam, there were many transportation projects confronted with risks and affected project deliverables. Therefore, it is important to control the risks which may occur in transportation projects, especially in the construction phase. This study aims at investigating the significance of risks in transportation projects through two main dimensions of risks, including the probability of occurrence and the severity of impact. Management strategies for the top-five most important risk are suggested as a guideline for related stakeholders. The research findings would benefit practitioners as well as authorities set up suitable policies to ensure the success of transportation projects.

articleTitle: Modeling and harmonic calculation of three-phase half wave diode rectifier
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The static converters are widely used in industrial nowadays. They cause power quality problems, especially harmonics. In sizing the systems which contain the static converters, the constraint of harmonics is indispensable. To calculate the harmonics, the Fourier transform of state equations can be applied. However, it is necessary to know the switching instants of semiconductors and the value of state variables at that time. It is difficult to determine the switching instants of semiconductors which have natural commutation (non-controlled). By using the switching criterions, which concern the currents and voltages of the semiconductors that change of operating state. The current or voltage of non-controlled semiconductors is canceled at their switching instants. These switching criterions constitute a set of implicit equations. In the papers, the authors present how to build and to solve these equations, and to calculate the harmonics generated by the static converters. Then, the authors apply on the three-phase half wave diode rectifier.

articleTitle: Inductance Calculation of Flux Intensifying PMa-SynRM by Equivalent Magnetic Circuit
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper presents the process to build an equivalent magnetic circuit (EMC) model for flux intensifying permanent magnet-assisted synchronous reluctance motor (FI-PMa-SynRM) so that the inductances can be calculated. The EMC model of the FI-PMa-SynRM is composed of the models for the stator and rotor cores, air-gap, and flux barriers, and it is then transformed to d- and q-axis frame. This conducts the calculation of d- and q-axis inductances. In addition, an interactive operation is applied to achieve the representative permeability and operational points of electrical steels so that more accurate values are obtained. The concordance of the calculated and simulated values shows the accuracy of the developed EMC model. The experiment is also employed to verify the feasibility of the EMC model.

articleTitle: Study on synthesis and structural characterization of ZnO-doped g-C3N4 materials for treatment of ciprofloxacin antibiotic in water
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Recently, the overuse and misuse of antibiotics are key factors leading to many negative problems to human and environment. Therefore, the removal for the antibiotics is very necessary, and photocatalysis is a highly efficient and environmentally friendly treatment method. Graphite carbon nitride <tex>$(\mathrm{g}-\mathrm{C}_{3}\mathrm{N}_{4})$</tex> is an organic semiconductor, researched to create a “new-generation” photocatalytic material system by hybridization with semiconductors such as TiO<inf>2</inf> and ZnO, which offers potential energy in the decomposition of organic compounds using the energy of visible light. In this study, ZnO/g-C3N4 materials were synthesized and characterized by advanced techniques, then apply for ciprofloxacin antibiotic (CIP) treatment. The CIP degradation efficiency of the material reached 84.36% and after three times the material was regenerated, ZnO/g-C3N4 composite still showed excellent degradation ability. Therefore, ZnO/g-C3N4 materials can be applied in environmental remediation and many other fields.

articleTitle: A Non-Contact Heart Rate Measurement System Based On LSTM Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The proposed method combines a non-contact measuring device with an LSTM neural network to provide a simple and precise wireless system to measure heart rate. The movement of the thoracic surface is modeled from the effects of breathing motion and cardiac contractility. Then, we generate a dataset for training the model. Finally, the trained model is used to derive heart rate estimates from medical radar data. These estimates are evaluated through Root Mean Square Error and Heart Rate Error Average.

articleTitle: Effect of waste red brick powder on fresh properties and strength development of cement paste
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study aims to assess the fresh properties and strength development of an environmentally friendly paste produced with waste red brick powder (WRP) as partial cement replacement. The WRP was collected from construction demolished waste (CDW) and ground into fine particles (<75μm). The paste samples were prepared with different WRP amounts (0%, 10%, 20%, 30% and 40<sup>%</sup>) of total binder weight and the water to binder (w/b) ratio was fixed at 0.5. The flowability, fresh unit weight and setting time were used to examine the fresh properties, while the compressive strength, flexural strength and ultrasonic pulse velocity (UPV) were conducted to examine the mechanical properties of paste specimens. Incorporating WRP reduced the flowability and fresh unit weight of paste samples, while the setting time increased with a higher amount of WRP content. The 28-day compressive strength and flexural strength were improved with 10% WRP content and reduced with a high WRP content. However, the inclusion of WRP reduced the UPV results of paste samples.

articleTitle: Study of self-healing cement based material using Bacillus Pseudojirmus bacteria
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Recent studies in the field of self healing materials have shown the potential of using bacteria for self-healing capacibility. However, some specific types of bacteria may be considered for use. This paper aims to study the self-healing ability when using Bacillus pseudofirmus with the concentration 10<sup>8</sup> CFU/mL. Series of compression tests and bending tests were performed on mortar samples with different bacterial contents of 5% and 10% to investigate the influence of bateria on the compressive strength and flexural strength of mortar samples. The results showed that compressive strength of mortar samples increased with bacterial content. The flexural strength of the 10<sup>%</sup> bacteria sample at age of 14 days was approximately 30% higher than that of the standard mortar sample at the same age. The cracked mortar samples were cured in water containing 5% and 10<sup>%</sup>Bacillus pseudofirmus solution, respectively to study the self-healing effect. According to preliminary findings, after 28 days of curing, calcite appeared around the cracked zone and filled cracks with a width up to 0.6mm. Experimental results showed that using Bacillus pseudofirmus in cementitious material was found to be a pratical approach for the purpose of self-healing.

articleTitle: Design of FPGA Logic for District Heating Pipe Damage Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: An automatic inspection system that predicts and analyzes damage to district heating pipe in advance is necessary because a rupture of district heating pipe buried in downtown can cause serious accidents such as casualties. In this paper, the TDR instrument was used to predict the damage of district heating pipe. Conventional TDR(Time Domain Reflectometry) instrument has disadvantages such as complexity and high cost. To compensate for these shortcomings, we developed a distributed TDR instrument using FPGA and checked the measurement results through a viewer program made using MFC(Microsoft Foundation Classes).

articleTitle: Assessment of solid waste collection system – A case study in Hai Chau district, Danang city, Vietnam
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Over the last decade, urgent problems related to the waste management system of Da Nang city have been recognized. Therefore, research on the current status of solid waste management system and solid waste collection system is gradually becoming paramount. This study applied Geographic Information System (GIS) and Global Positioning System (GPS) to study the current status of the waste collection system in Hai Chau district, Danang city. The GPS devices were utilized and in-depth interviews were also performed to collect information and data about the waste collection system. Data were synthesized, processed, and analyzed by QGIS 3.4 and Excel 2016. Four teams were in charge of solid waste collection in the entire Hai Chau district. The average daily amounts of solid waste collected were 56t (Team 1), 42.4t (Team 2), 42.6t (Team 3), and 61.1t (Team 4). The coverage ratios and physical duplication ratios of the three teams were 36.5% and 51.1% (Team 1), 55.6% and 47.1% (Team 2), 51.4% and 34.4% (Team 3). The compaction truck of Team 4 only transferred solid waste from transfer station to Khanh Son landfill. The problems and challenges of the solid waste collection system were also highlighted with recommendations for the outcomes.

articleTitle: Using the LQI2R Control Method on the Adaptive Cruise Control System for a Platoon of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Autonomous vehicles refer to vehicles whose operations and actuations are directed towards fully controlled. However, we need a long transition period where drivers of vehicles with different levels of partial automation will be responsible for the driving function. The Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) is one of the key subsystems of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems that have attracted considerable research and development efforts due to their multifaceted advantages such as increasing the urban arterial capacity, improve traffic safety with shorter inter-vehicle spacing between vehicles [1], [2]. This study proposes a Linear Quadratic Integral Regulator with double integrator (LQI<sup>2</sup>R) for ACC technology in a platoon by using radars. An important criterion in ACC controller design is string stability which is analyzed by using a frequency-domain approach and Nyquist diagram within considering the different values of the constant headway time. The main purpose of platoon control is to keep the desired inter-vehicle distance while guaranteeing string stability requirements. The numerical simulations are carried out to validate the effectiveness of our results.

articleTitle: LPV observer for leakage detection of the pipeline system
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This work presents a Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) observer for the leak diagnosis problem in a water pipeline system. First, the LPV representation of the system is derived from the nonlinear model of a pipeline. Then LPV observer is designed via solving Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs). To assess the performance of the proposed approach, the proposed observer is applied to detect the leak of a real pipeline system. Both simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Autonomous Mobile Robot: Navigating and Monitoring Fire Safety at Power Substations
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper presents a computer vision application using Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR) to monitor fire safety at power substations. The system utilizes satellite and IMU-based robot navigation along with computer vision to allow an AMR to patrol and monitor fire safety. The smoke and fire detection model, with an mAP of 82.71%, is deployed on cloud and infers online during the robot navigation. Navigating at a 220/110 kV power substation in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, we achieved a 3D error of satellite-based localization of less than 10cm and an orientation error below 0.2rad.

articleTitle: Economic Analysis wind/photovoltaic for Grid-Connected System in Vietnam
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper presents a method to economic analyst the wind/Photovoltaic hybrid system connected to the grid for local Vung Tau city in Vietnam. A typical residential load is selected to simulate situations where Photovoltaic/wind and Photovoltaic/wind/battery hybrid system connected to grid. Furthermore, Homer software is used for simulation both electric production and economic output as well as extracting solar irradiance and wind speed. The results of economic feasibility study show that the cost of Energy in range 0.02 USD/kWh to 0.12 USD/kWh and Net Present Cost ranging from 2000USD to 6,000USD.

articleTitle: PLC-based PID control system design for an air levitation system
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The paper provides a study of a PID controller to stabilize a ball in the air levitation system. First, the nonlinear model of the system is developed to capture the behavior of the system. Then the nonlinear model is linearized at the equilibrium of the system via Taylor's theorem. The parameters of the linearized model are identified through the experimental data collected from a real air levitation system. Based on the linearized model, the PID control is designed to control the ball stabilizing at the working point. Both the simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Studying the drag coefficient of three-wheel electrical car
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The electric car has drawn the attention of many researchers and car manufacturers because of the fossil fuel depletion and environmental pollution. Moreover, Vietnam is a low-income country, and transportation infrastructure has not really developed. Therefore, the development of three-wheel electric car is appropriate and necessary. Optimizing the body car's aerodynamics plays a very important role in improving energy efficiency. In this project, we design and optimize the body of a three-wheel electrical car using Solid Flow Simulation to obtain a better drag coefficient (C<inf>d</inf>) value. The initial simulated-condition set to 35 km/h of air velocity. Based on the surface-pressure distribution after simulating, the preliminary design of the body has been modified. The simulation results reveal that the drag coefficient has decreased from 0,5 to 0,39. The optimized C<inf>d</inf> value is relatively small and agrees with the standard's value varying from 0,32 to 0,52 for the typical Sedan cars. The optimal electric car body design will be built and tested. Furthermore, the results also suggest the applicability of Solid Flow Simulation to design and manufacture car components.

articleTitle: Study on Design of automatic Noise measurement Sensor on the based of IoT Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this paper, we conduct research on the design of a noise sensor that collects noise from the microphone and converts it to an analog electrical signal, which will be put into a signal generator circuit (Transmitter) to filter noise and amplify it. Then this electrical signal will be fed into the analog to digital signal converter (ADC) circuit, then the digital signal will be fed into the digital signal processing circuit (DSP) to calculate the level of noise in dBA form. Then the developer will integrate the noise sensor into the system, and just read the value of the registers inside the DSP processor to get the noise value through RS485 communication. The noise sensor is designed using STMicroelectronics ARM STM32F407 microcontroller to communicate with Microphone IM69D130 through I<sup>2</sup>S standard, and use the Fast Fourier Transformer algorithm to process DSP block instructions. The obtained test results can be compared with some other noise measuring devices that have verified the success of the proposed solution in this study.

articleTitle: Motion planning of four-wheeled omnidirectional robots in a NMPC framework
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This work presents a safe navigation of mobile autonomous robot, more specifically, four-wheeled omnidirectional robot. The contribution lies in applying an NMPC (Nonlinear Model Predictive Control) for the two different dynamic models of four-wheeled omnidirectional robot in the specified working space. Some important criteria such as computational time, length of trajectory and the capacity of obstacle avoidance are used to compare through simulation with the goal of sticking out which dynamic model is the best in a specified context.

articleTitle: Qualitfication and Optimization of the Capacior Position for Distribution Network with Harmonics by genetic Algorith
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper presents the calculation method and optimal compensation capacity of the capacitor considering the harmonics of the nonlinear load in the distribution network. The objective function of minimizing power loss in the considered time period is bound to ensure the operation requirements of the distribution grid. This paper uses genetic algorithm (GA - Genetic Algorithm) to select the position and capacity of capacitors, reduce harmonics as an optimal solution to help solving practical problems in grid operation. The content of the article will apply Matlab to model and simulate the local distribution grid, simulate to improve the practicality of the calculation results. The results allow comparing voltage quality with harmonic power loss on the grid before and after compensating.

articleTitle: Investigating the ultimate bending strength of reinforced concrete section under different non-linear constitutive models according to the design standard TCVN 5574–2018
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this study, we present the non-linear deformation models of concrete used in the last updated Vietnamese design standard TCVN 5574–2018 related to the design. A computational procedure is proposed for analyzing the ultimate state of reinforced concrete section and calculating its ultimate bending strength, including the case of multi-layered reinforced section. This procedure is then successfully implemented in the Python programming language to analyze in detail the state of materials (strain, stress, force in the concrete and steel). The ultimate bending moment is also determined. Different scenario of beam section, percentage ratio of reinforcement and non-linear models are investigated.

articleTitle: Evaluation of natural xanthones for the development of new drugs to treat Alzheimer's disease by computational chemistry
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The enzyme acetylcholinesterase (AChE) is crucial in the management of Alzheimer's disease. Acetylcholine is hydrolyzed by AChE, which prevents the conduction of nerve impulses. Potential sources of compounds that block the AChE enzyme include natural herbs. In this investigation, we assessed the ability of 100 natural xanthones to inhibit AChE in comparison to commercially available controls (donepezil and tacrine) for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease by using the docking and ADME approaches. According to research findings, the interaction energies of xanthones 21, 24, 55,67, 68, 118, and 120 with proteins were favorable. These compounds were compatible with Lipinski's rule and exhibited advantageous pharmacological characteristics, particularly in compound 120. Hence, 120 may be a potential candidate for the development of new drugs for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.

articleTitle: An Interpretable Machine Learning Approach For Fault Classification in Bearing Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper presents an interpretable machine learning approach to classify different types of faults in ball bearing systems with high accuracy. These methods are based on ensemble methods (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and AdaBoost) which use data from the fan system collected by vibration monitors mounted on three axes. The proposed technique needs statistical feature inputs to classify different types of faults. We train models and explain their output using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations). In the rigorous numerical study, we point out a suitable explanation for black-box predictive models trained on vibration data. Our model achieves 98 percent classification accuracy when classifying all fault types.

articleTitle: Diagnosing Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Based on Breathing Sound Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Breathing sound is a characteristic indicator of human health. Each type of respiratory disease will have its own distinct breathing sounds. Therefore, breathing sounds can be used to identify some respiratory diseases. In this paper, we propose a breathing sound classification method to diagnose Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease using wavelet transform and transfer learning technique. Breathing sounds are divided into breathing cycles. These breathing cycles are analyzed using multiple wavelet families and spectral transformations to represent the signal then use machine learning classification algorithms including VGG16, ResNet50, InceptionV3for classification. The best Wavelet family classification results give an accuracy of up to 99.54%.

articleTitle: Air Pollution Prediction Using Deep Learning and EEMD
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Air pollution has become a hot topic in our society in recent years. Prediction of air pollution is necessary to give early warnings to the community to prevent affecting public. In this work, we utilized ensemble empirical mode decomposition and Long-short term memory to build AI model for 2 hours-ahead PM2.5 concentration prediction. Our work comprises mainly two steps: first, decomposing time-series data into intrinsic features; and one model Long-short term memory is used to learn pattern from training data. The experimental results show that our work outperform the baseline models and significantly improve the performance in term of RMSE and IOA.

articleTitle: Effect of ground granulated blast furnace slag and fly ash on mechanical properties and sulfate attack resistance of fine-grained concrete using sea sand
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper presents study results on the effects of ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) and fly ash (FA) on the slump, mechanical properties, absorption, and sulfate resistance of fine-grained concrete using sea sand (FGCSS). Seven types of fine gained-concretes (FGC) with W/ B ratios of 0.38 were prepared including: FGC for reference that use cement and treated sea sand (FGCR), FGC for reference that use cement and sea sand (FGCR-SS), three types of FGCSS that use GGBFS as a substitution for cement and two type of FGCSS that use both GGBFS and FA. The aggregate used consists of river sand with a modulus of fineness 2.77 and sea sand (SS) with a modulus of fineness 1.05. The study results showed that FGCR-SS had an increase in strength compared to FGCR at 7, 28 days but had a lower decrease in strength compared to FGCR at 90 days. FGCSSs using GGBFS to replace cement by 30-50% showed an improvement in compressive strength and splitting tensile strength at all experimental ages. For FGCSSs using both GGBFS and FA, a replacement of 35%GGBFS and 15%FA also showed an improvement in the compressive strength and splitting tensile strength from 28 days later. FGCR-SS showed 3.15 times more expansion than FGCR at 180 days. The use of GGBFS and FA in FGCSS significantly reduced sulfate expansion compared with that of FGCR-SS; at 180 days, the sulfate expansion of both FGC using 70% GGBFS and FGC using a combination of 35% GGBFS and 15% FA was almost similar to that of FGCR.

articleTitle: Four Mode Demultiplexer Based on Branched Silicon Waveguides For Photonics Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a proof-of-concept of a broadband four-mode demultiplexer via numerical simulation of both device and system levels. The device allows simultaneous operation of four guided modes by designing optimally the tilted branches from a straightforward bus waveguide thanks to utilizing the phase-matching technique. Simulation results show that the device has a good figure-of-merit with insertion loss is not exceeded 1.1dB absolutely and crosstalk is always smaller than -18dB in 100nm-wavelength bandwidth of C-band for all four modes. Moreover, the designed device also has large geometry tolerances, which correspond to height and width tolerances up to Ah = ± 10nm and ΔW = ± 15nm in 100nm-wavelength bandwidth, respectively. Simulation results in the level of communication system also demonstrate that a total capacity of as much as 4×40Gbps can be reached with the BER quality is lower than 10–<sup>9</sup> in a broad-wavelength band of 100nm of C-band. Such advantages of the good performance besides ultra-compactness thus make the device a promising candidate for popular applications in on-chip photonics interconnects as well as high-speed communication-integrated systems.

articleTitle: Green tourism planning for Danang City after COVID-19, vision to 2050
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Danang city is known as the most attractive tourist city in Vietnam as well as in the world. Danang possesses rich and diverse natural resources, urban space facing the river, sea, alternating hilly areas creating an urban structure that is both the modern and the natural. In addition, Danang has won the Vietnam ICT Index award for 12 consecutive years because of its smart, modern, and effective digital technology system in linking and supporting tourism development with the neighboring localities. However, the outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic had caused millions of deaths in the most countries worldwide since 2019. Leading to the economic activities, the trade in services, tourism, transportation, etc... have all been seriously affected, even stopped working together for a long time. After that, the appearance of vaccines has partly controlled the epidemic situation. But people's living habits and views relating the tourism have changed significantly. Thus, the trend of “green tourism country - slow tourism” is being strongly responded by tourists after the Covid-19 pandemic. This is explained that the tourists will travel in small groups, enjoy travel experiences close to nature, immerse themselves in the culture of indigenous people, and combine with local sports activities. Therefore, the authors propose a model of “diffusion planning” to effectively solve the problems in “Green tourism planning for Danang City after COVID-19, vision to 2050” to contribute to the orientation of sustainable tourism development in Danang city.

articleTitle: Loosely Coupled GPS/INS Integration for Road Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: With the development of MEMS sensors, IMUs are used in many fields thanks to their compactness, as well as the high demand for determining the rotation angle and position of objects. However, for applications that require high accuracy, IMU does not meet the quality because of the accumulation of INS's error over time caused by measurement error. Therefore, to be able to apply IMU to positioning problems, it requires an absolute positioning system to reset the error of the INS. The paper will focus on building a loosely coupled GPS/INS integration algorithm and evaluating the estimated results of the system when experiencing GPS signal jamming. In addition, we will build a three-axis orientation estimation algorithm to improve the estimated results of the GPS/INS system. Experiment results have shown that our proposed algorithm gives the RMS positioning error less than 5m when experiencing GPS signal jamming for 10s. The RMS error of all three angles is less than 2°.

articleTitle: Classifying Laboratory Tools using Robot arm associated with Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2022 7th National Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: 6D pose estimation of 3D object is an important task in robotics, which allows the robot to determine object's position and orientation in pick-and-place applications. This paper proposes a solution for 6D pose estimation using RGB-D camera and 6-DOF robot. The main algorithm is the Point Pair Feature (PPF) that helps to find the position and orientation of the object. The authors also give some improvements based on the original algorithm. The accuracy of PPF algorithm's will be evaluated in 5°, 5cm. For communication between the robot and the computer, we build a UDP-based protocol program that is suggested by Yaskawa. In addition, we provide a Graphical User Interface (GUI) to support the control and observation of the execution.
